description: Closed form for the structural pole-prefactor α_3 at H_3(R, q): α_3(q) = h·z² + z.  Trust profile {axiom: 4, derived: 3, computational: 1} — the four first-principles axioms (Hecke energy + Schur + Wedderburn + finite-Jones), three derived steps (r_k construction, Wedderburn pairing, closed form), and one COMPUTATIONAL leaf evaluating at q_0 against the existing `alpha-k-jones-markov-h3.witness.json` witness.  Generated by `build_alpha_k_h3_chains.py`.

steps.name: Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_3(R, q)
steps.operation: Define H_3(R, q) as the unital R-algebra generated by σ_1, σ_2 modulo the Hecke quadratic σ_i² = (q − q⁻¹)·σ_i + 1 and the braid relation σ_1·σ_2·σ_1 = σ_2·σ_1·σ_2.  The (q − q⁻¹) coefficient is the per-crossing Hecke energy.

steps.name: Irrep classification — partitions of 3
steps.operation: By Schur, the irreducible reps of H_3(R, q) are in bijection with partitions λ ⊢ 3 (Schur–Weyl duality deforming the symmetric-group case): Λ = {(3), (2,1), (1,1,1)}, with q-dimensions 1, 2, 1.

steps.name: Wedderburn block decomposition
steps.operation: By Wedderburn, H_3(R, q) ≅ ⊕_λ M_{f_λ}(K(q)) where f_λ = #SYT(λ).  The Markov trace decomposes uniquely as tr_M(β) = Σ_λ y_λ · χ_λ(β), with central scalars y_λ (Jones–Markov weights).
steps.output_value: tr_M = Σ_{λ ⊢ 3}  y_λ · χ_λ  on H_3(R, q)

steps.name: Finite-Jones uniqueness of the Markov trace
steps.operation: By the finite-Jones existence/uniqueness theorem, the Markov-trace conditions tr_M(1) = 1, tr_M(σ_i α) = z·tr_M(α), and Markov stabilisation determine the Jones–Markov weights y_λ uniquely: solve a 3×3 linear system in (y_(3), y_(2,1), y_(1,1,1)) using the three trace values tr_M(1), tr_M(σ_1), tr_M(σ_1·σ_2) which evaluate as (1, z, z²) by stabilisation.
steps.output_value: y_λ uniquely determined by (tr_M(1), tr_M(σ_1), tr_M(σ_1σ_2)) = (1, z, z²)

steps.name: Depth-3 word representative r_3
steps.operation: Choose r_3 as a canonical word (or linear combination) in the braid generators σ_1, σ_2 such that the Markov trace tr_M(r_3) directly extracts the depth-3 prefactor α_3.  Concrete choice: r_3 = σ_1·σ_2·σ_1 (the longest alternating word in B_3; tr_M(r_3) = h·z² + z under the Markov-trace pairing, giving α_3).
steps.output_value: r_3 = σ_1·σ_2·σ_1 (the longest alternating word in B_3; tr_M(r_3) = h·z² + z under the Markov-trace pairing, giving α_3).

steps.name: Definition α_3 := tr_M(r_3)
steps.operation: Define α_3 as the Markov trace of r_3.  Expanded via the Wedderburn block decomposition (step 3), this is α_3 = Σ_{λ ⊢ 3} y_λ · χ_λ(r_3).  This is the algebraic definition; the depth-3 interpretation comes from the canonical word choice in step 5.

steps.name: Closed form  α_3 = h·z² + z
steps.operation: Pure algebra in z and h: α_3 = tr_M(σ_1·σ_2·σ_1).  Decompose σ_1·σ_2·σ_1 in the Hecke algebra: σ_1·σ_2·σ_1 = σ_2·σ_1·σ_2 (braid relation), and using σ_i² = h·σ_i + 1 (Hecke quadratic, h = q − q⁻¹) plus Markov stabilisation, the trace evaluates as h·z² + z.  This is the depth-3 alternating-word stratum.  Physical identification: Jet-prefix / chirality-knot stratum (e.g. 6_1).
